reviewer: model visual review of the rendered block layout
authority: none - review artifact only; output.json remains authoritative
verdict: not yet spatially coherent - two placement contradictions must be resolved before Stage 05

checks.accessibility: pass - closure_member_access_region and disturbance_region render outside the shell; the release surface is reachable
checks.user_reachability: pass - the detent and the closure sit on the same outward face, so one hand reaches both
checks.enclosure_consistency: pass - the shell bounds all interior regions; the closure forms part of the boundary rather than floating inside it
checks.swept_volume_conflicts: pass - the closure arc extends outward beyond the shell, which is correct for an outward-opening lid, and clears the storage volume
checks.serviceability: pass - no separate cover is drawn; the closure itself is the service opening
checks.assembly_feasibility: concern - the opening_stop is drawn at the far end from both the hinge and the closure, so the piece that limits the swing does not touch what swings
checks.packaging: pass - the storage volume occupies the core and nothing intrudes into it

findings.concern: The hinge and the closure it carries are on opposite sides of the product. opening_interface renders as a tall slab on the left flank; closure_member renders on the right boundary face. A hinge must attach to the closure it hinges.
findings.why_the_json_missed_it: The blueprint records 'closure_member guidance <- opening_interface' and a parallel placement, but zone assignment is independent: the obligation put the hinge in FLANKING while the closure is in BOUNDARY. Nothing in the schema forces a reactor to be adjacent to what it reacts.
findings.missing_information: zones express distance from the primary axis but not adjacency; a support placed to react an obligation must be co-located with the element it serves

findings.concern: opening_stop is placed at the bottom end of the primary axis, remote from the hinge line and the closure. A travel stop that does not meet the moving element cannot limit it.
findings.why_the_json_missed_it: The TRAVEL_LIMIT obligation maps to zone END, and END is a single zone with no statement of which end, nor of which element it must meet.
findings.missing_information: the END zone does not distinguish the two ends of the primary axis, and carries no adjacency to the element it bounds

findings.concern: BOUNDARY does not say which face. The closure and the detent are drawn on the same side face; for a storage box a lid would normally be the top face and the catch the front. The renderer chose a face the blueprint never specified.
findings.missing_information: no face identity (top/front/side) on boundary placements

confirmed_from_blueprint: closure_member and opening_interface swept arcs overlap the retention and travel-limit regions (2 unresolved interference candidates) - visible as overlapping pale envelopes
